verdict: Charles River's profit jumped to $333M only because a one-off $246M tax-reserve reversal flattered the quarter, while reported revenue fell 2% on divestitures even as underlying organic sales grew 5%.

kpis.label: Revenue
kpis.note: -2.2% YoY reported, vs $1,005M a year ago; +4.7% organic (stripping out deals, divestitures and currency)

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: vs $1.10 a year ago — includes a $5.06 one-off tax benefit (see one-offs)

kpis.label: EPS (non-GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: +27% YoY — the company's underlying measure, leaving out the tax reversal and deal items

kpis.label: Tax-reserve reversal benefit
kpis.note: One-off gain from reversing acquired tax reserves — $201M in the tax line plus $45M in running costs

segments.name: Discovery and Safety Assessment (DSA)
segments.note: Testing new drugs for safety before human trials — the largest business. Reported revenue fell 1% after divesting some European sites, but organic revenue rose 6% on higher safety-assessment study volume.

segments.name: Research Models and Services (RMS)
segments.note: Research models (animals bred for labs) and related services. Reported revenue fell 3% after the Cell Solutions divestiture; organic revenue fell 1% on softer demand for large research models.

segments.name: Manufacturing Solutions
segments.note: Making and testing biologic medicines and keeping labs sterile and safe. Reported revenue fell 6% after the CDMO divestiture (contract drug manufacturing); organic revenue rose 7% on strong biologics testing and microbial solutions demand.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Selling and running the company. Down sharply from $178M a year ago, helped by a $45M reversal of non-income tax reserves in DSA (see one-offs). Shown as $140M so the rounded lines tie — exact figure $140.6M.

opex.name: Amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of intangible assets bought in past deals, such as customer relationships, over their useful lives. Down from $27M a year ago after divestitures.

otherDetail: A net $32M cost below operating profit: interest expense of $29M, less $1M of interest income, plus $4M of other expense, net.
follow100Note: The tax row adds money this quarter instead of taking it: the tax-reserve reversal turned the tax line into a large benefit, which is why profit looks so high next to operating income.

takeaways.title: A one-off tax reversal made the quarter
takeaways.text: Reversing acquired tax reserves — after newly enacted tax legislation and completing tax requirements in a foreign jurisdiction — added $245.6M, or $5.06 per share: a $201M benefit inside the tax line and a $44.6M benefit inside DSA running costs. That is why GAAP EPS was $6.86 while the company's non-GAAP EPS, which leaves the reversal out, was $3.09.

takeaways.title: Underlying sales grew; reported sales fell
takeaways.text: Reported revenue fell 2.2% to $982.7M because of the May 2026 divestitures (the CDMO and Cell Solutions businesses and some European Discovery sites). On an organic basis revenue rose 4.7% — DSA up 5.9% and Manufacturing up 7.4%, partly offset by RMS down 0.6%.

takeaways.title: Core earnings still improved
takeaways.text: Even without the tax reversal, non-GAAP EPS rose 27% to $3.09 and the non-GAAP operating margin widened to 23.0% from 19.7%, helped by the CDMO divestiture and more safety-assessment work. Consolidated net income was $334M ($333M attributable to shareholders), vs $56M a year ago, and the company raised its 2026 guidance.

oneTimers: The quarter includes a $245.6M benefit ($5.06 per diluted share) from reversing acquired tax reserves, following newly enacted tax legislation clarifying the company's obligations and completion of certain tax requirements in a foreign jurisdiction: $201M was recognised as a benefit in the tax line — turning it into a $163.8M benefit for the quarter — and $44.6M as a benefit in selling, general and administrative costs for non-income tax reserves. The company treats it as one-off and excludes it from non-GAAP results.
footerNote: In thousands, rounded to $M; SG&A shown as $140M (exact $140.6M), tax benefit as $163M (exact $163.8M), so lines tie.
